title: Harvey Accelerates Enterprise AI with Agent-Powered Platform and Microsoft 365 Copilot
author: Harvey Team

dom.t: Vertical AI: Commercial traction cannot prove defensibility

st.t: Vertical AI: Commercial traction cannot prove defensibility
st.an: The source supports the cluster’s application-layer and embedded-workflow account by presenting Harvey’s legal assistance inside Microsoft 365 Copilot, grounded in the user’s active document or email and extending across research, analysis and drafting. It also fits the cluster’s evidentiary caution: the announcement asserts accurate, trusted answers but provides no measured evidence of legal performance, productivity or durable competitive advantage.
qs: Responses are delivered inline within Copilot and grounded in the document, email, or item in focus, reducing the need to switch systems.

kp.k: Copilot integration embeds legal AI in existing workflows
kp.d: In its March 4, 2026 announcement, Harvey describes an expanded Microsoft partnership and a planned integration allowing legal professionals to access Harvey Assistant within Microsoft 365 Copilot. Users would invoke @Harvey or select its agent to receive inline responses grounded in the document, email or item in focus. Harvey presents reduced switching between systems as a benefit; the initial integration is scheduled to launch in Q2 2026.
qs: By mentioning @Harvey in Copilot or selecting the agent from the Copilot agents menu, users can query the Harvey Assistant to analyze agreements, research market terms, identify negotiation positions, and retrieve precedent from systems powered by Harvey.
Responses are delivered inline within Copilot and grounded in the document, email, or item in focus, reducing the need to switch systems.
Harvey’s initial integration with Microsoft 365 Copilot will launch in Q2 2026.

kp.k: Assistance spans agreement analysis, drafting and closing documentation
kp.d: Harvey describes support across legal matter workflows: agreement analysis, market-term research, negotiation-position identification and precedent retrieval, followed by drafting and refinement in Word, business-facing summaries, counterparty-response analysis and closing memoranda. These are announced capabilities, rather than reported findings about lawyer productivity or outcomes.
qs: As matters progress, users can draft and refine documents in Word, generate executive summaries for business stakeholders, analyze counterparty responses, and produce closing memoranda that capture negotiated changes and preserve precedent value.

kp.k: Advanced workflows transfer to Harvey with context preserved
kp.d: The announcement distinguishes inline Copilot assistance from advanced document analysis and structured legal workflows conducted in Harvey. A “View in Harvey” function is described as transferring the conversation together with relevant documents and context, enabling continuity between the two environments.
qs: For advanced document analysis or structured legal workflows, a “View in Harvey” function transfers the conversation thread into Harvey with relevant documents and context preserved.

kp.k: Accuracy and trust are asserted benefits
kp.d: Harvey claims the integration will deliver accurate answers instantly, while CEO and co-founder Winston Weinberg characterizes the answers as trusted and emphasizes lawyers remaining within familiar tools. These are vendor assertions in the announcement, which supplies no accuracy measurements or verification procedures.
qs: The integration enables lawyers to ask legal questions in Copilot, receive accurate answers instantly, and move from initial inquiries to deeper analysis and execution within their existing workflow.

By bringing Harvey’s legal intelligence directly into Copilot, we’re enabling lawyers to ask legal questions, get trusted answers, and stay in the flow of their work, without leaving the tools they already rely on.

kp.k: Harvey plans internal adoption to align with enterprise buyers
kp.d: Beyond the customer-facing integration, Harvey states that it will use Microsoft 365 and Copilot for its own internal workflows and go-to-market activities, explicitly linking this adoption to alignment with enterprise buyers.
qs: In addition to the integration, Harvey will use Microsoft 365 and Copilot across its internal workflows and go to market motions to align with enterprise buyers.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: The Harvey Team claims its planned Microsoft 365 Copilot integration will give lawyers precise, precedent-aware legal answers within their existing Microsoft workflow, reducing switching between systems.
pts.d: The announcement describes users invoking Harvey through an @Harvey mention or the Copilot agents menu to analyze agreements, research market terms, identify negotiation positions and retrieve precedent. Answers are said to be grounded in the document, email or item in focus. It characterizes answers as accurate and instant. These are the Harvey Team's product capability claims, framed as assistance to lawyers rather than replacement of lawyers or autonomous delivery of legal services.

pts.k: The Harvey Team claims the integration will support successive stages of legal matters, including drafting, negotiation analysis, stakeholder reporting and preservation of precedent.
pts.d: The source describes drafting and refinement in Word, executive summaries, analysis of counterparty responses and closing memoranda recording negotiated changes. It also claims users can transfer the conversation to Harvey for advanced analysis or structured workflows while retaining documents and context. The claimed change is continuity across legal tasks and applications; the source does not quantify time or cost savings.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source offers a first-party product announcement and executive endorsements, not measured evidence of accuracy or workflow improvements.
pts.d: The Harvey Team describes intended functionality and includes supporting statements from Harvey CEO Winston Weinberg and Microsoft commercial-business CEO Judson Althoff. These statements supply vendor authority and rationale, rather than independent validation. The document supplies no benchmarks, accuracy measurements, customer cases, observed deployment results or quantified productivity gains supporting its claims of precise, trusted or instant answers.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The March 4, 2026 announcement schedules the initial integration for Q2 2026; the described benefits depend on using the integrated Copilot–Harvey workflow.
pts.d: Although much of the functionality is described in the present tense, the source says the integration is being built and gives a future initial launch date. It does not provide separate release dates for individual capabilities. Users invoke Harvey within Copilot; precedent retrieval is described as coming from systems powered by Harvey, and advanced analysis or structured workflows involve transferring into Harvey. No accuracy qualifications or human-verification requirements are stated.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The stated beneficiaries are lawyers and legal teams using Microsoft 365, with business stakeholders receiving summaries; Harvey also announces its own internal adoption.
pts.d: Legal professionals are expected to receive specialized legal assistance inside familiar applications and retain context when moving to Harvey. Business stakeholders are identified as recipients of executive summaries. The enterprise-oriented announcement does not distinguish law-firm users from in-house legal departments or predict changes in staffing, fees or public access to legal help. Separately, the Harvey Team says Harvey will use Microsoft 365 and Copilot internally and in go-to-market activities to align with enterprise buyers.
